place_info.title: Iron Works Barbecue
place_info.address: 100 Red River St, Austin, TX 78701, United States

reviews.snippet:
Iron Works is a great, low key restaurant in the downtown area. The staff are so friendly and went out of their way to help and make the place feel welcoming.

The BBQ was a bit dry. The ribs had great taste but was very dry on the edges. The brisket and sausage was also dry but dipped in the BBQ sauce well.

No AC in the building but they utilized fans well to keep the air moving. Sitting outside was relaxing.

Enjoyed it! Was fun to look at the celebrities that have visited and the historical pieces.

reviews.snippet: Good barbecue joint. This was between my hotel and my conference and I stopped in here for an early dinner. I got a pulled pork plate with coleslaw and green beans (and a couple of slices of white bread) and a sweet tea. The outdoor seating is very nice - overlooking the newly finished pathway along Waller creek. I would not characterize the portions as generous. They’re ok and probably appropriate for most. I enjoyed it and can recommend.

reviews.snippet:
Came into this spot because average rating was decent and we've been to all the top 6-7 spots in the immediate Austin area already. Figured try something new and see why so many 5 star ratings. Around 4:45pm on a Friday...not a soul in sight.

This was barely 1 star for us. Each meat was wrong. Brisket dry, zero fat. Rib so oily and chewy could barely pull off the bone. Turkey was over smoked. Sausage was run of the mill...filling was reminiscent of just a hot dog fill. Every side lacked flavor and freshness. Green beans mushy, slaw so runny it was dripping, bbq beans we're tasteless. Not sure why add the pickles and onions it added nothing to the plates. The only decent side was creamed corn as it had some flavor. All this was $80+ dollars with a beer.

The pro is the spot is really neat inside and location is right downtown Austin. Our assumption after eating here is that the 5-star ratings are not for the food but atmosphere, location, and was probably a great spot for bbq back in the day? I guess to each there own and try if you want.

reviews.snippet:
Iron Works BBQ got it done—plain and simple. Coming from a New Yorker with only a day in Austin, I wasn’t about to stand on line for hours at the big-name spots. Walked into Iron Works, no nonsense, and walked out full and happy.

Yeah, I was bummed the beef ribs were sold out (heard they’re the move), but the brisket, fries, and all the trimmings came through strong. Smoky, flavorful, exactly what you want.

Crack open a Shiner Bock, grab a seat, and enjoy. No frills, just solid Texas BBQ on Dirty 6th. 👍

reviews.snippet: Came to IWB during SXSW during lunch time and the place was not busy at all. 🤨 Their service was super quick and it was reasonably priced. Read many good recommendations about Brisket, but it was not as juicy as what I was expecting. It was tender but drier and leaner. Knowing BBQ places in Dallas/Fort Worth region, it was a little disappointed. It was my first Brisket in Austin, let’s see how others are….

reviews.snippet:
We had a great experience at Iron Works Barbecue. The staff were friendly, welcoming, and made us feel right at home from the moment we arrived.

The food was delicious, and the service was impressively fast. Everything came out quickly without sacrificing quality.

We also really enjoyed the outdoor seating area. Even on a hot day, it felt comfortable thanks to the shade and the nice breeze, making it a pleasant place to relax and enjoy our meal.

Great food, great service, and a great atmosphere. We’d definitely come back the next time we’re in Austin.

reviews.snippet: This place has been serving BBQ since the early 70s. The building is old and has an even older history. I love that they have kept inside and out as original as possible. The service here was good with the staff being helpful and courteous throughout my visit. The food especially the brisket is tremendous. Sides were very good also. The only downside is the price has gone up and the value vs quantity ratio has dropped over the years. Overall great BBQ but pricy.
